I've been working this land for 50 years. I know this soil in Quzhou like I know my own hands. My farm is 3 mu — not big, but it's mine. I'm alone now, so I can't push myself too hard. My body isn't what it was at 40.

My wheat-maize land, I'll put 2 mu on that rotation. The other 1 mu I'll keep in cotton — I've grown cotton here since my 20s, I know when to water it, I know the bollworm. I won't change what I know how to do.

**Wheat:** I plant in October, the same week I always do. I use the improved Jimai variety the village has used for years — not the new expensive ones from the company, I don't trust what I don't know. I'll plough first, same as always. Three waterings: before winter sets in, then at jointing, then at heading. Two rounds of pesticide for rust and aphids. Fertilizer — I put down base fertilizer at planting and top-dress at jointing. I've learned not to over-fertilize, it lodges the stalks.

**Maize:** After wheat harvest in June I rotary-till quickly and get seed in the ground fast. I use hybrid seed for maize — even I switched to that maybe 25 years ago, the yields are better. Summer gets some rain, so I only irrigate twice unless it's dry. Not much pesticide trouble with summer maize usually.

**Cotton:** This is the hard one at my age. Picking is slow now. But I know cotton, so I keep 1 mu. I plough in spring, transplant or direct seed in late April. Cotton needs water at flowering and boll-setting. More pesticide than the other crops — bollworm, aphids, spider mites. I spray myself, carefully.
